_comment: Every acceptance criterion in macro-metrics docs/user-stories-frontend.md, and what
the .beh notation did with it. Generated by tmp/build-ledger.js; `text` is verbatim
from the source, extracted mechanically, so it cannot drift into what I remember the
AC saying. `node prose-audit.js` refuses if any AC is unaccounted for.
This file exists because the tempting way to report this experiment is a coverage
percentage over the ACs that happened to fit, which would have read 78% and meant
nothing. The denominator is the whole document or the number is theatre.

acs.text: On navigation to `/`, the page shell renders instantly: header, sticky mini-nav, section headings, and skeleton versions of all 9 preset ratio cards and all 3 indicator cards
acs.note: The three section headings are asserted. "all 9 preset + all 3 indicator skeletons" has no cardinality, and the skeletons are className-only <div>s with no accessible name. "renders instantly" is a timing claim with no expression.

acs.text: All 9 preset ratio fetches fire in parallel (`GET /api/metrics/ratio?numerator=X&denominator=Y`)
acs.note: Wire-level and concurrent; a behaviour tree has no honest way to own it.

acs.text: All 3 indicator fetches fire in parallel (`GET /api/metrics/{id}`)
acs.note: As above.

acs.text: As each response arrives, the corresponding skeleton is replaced by the real card — cards do not wait for all fetches to complete
acs.note: "As each response arrives" is a during-clause; "replaced by" needs an absence assertion; "cards do not wait" is a negative over a collection. Three missing shapes in one sentence.

acs.text: The sticky mini-nav contains three anchor links: **Presets**, **Compare**, **Indicators**
acs.note: FINDING (spec vs app): the AC says three "anchor links"; StickyNav.tsx renders three <button onClick={scrollIntoView}>. Encoded as link: so the generator reports the unbound noun rather than the corpus absorbing the divergence.

acs.text: Clicking a mini-nav anchor smoothly scrolls to the matching section
acs.note: No scroll verb and no viewport concept. `lands` asserts a URL, and scrollIntoView changes no URL and no DOM state, so there is nothing the notation could point at even in principle.

acs.text: The mini-nav remains visible (sticky) as the user scrolls
acs.note: Requires a scroll ACTION and a stays-visible assertion. Neither exists.

acs.text: Each loaded preset card displays: title, headline ratio value (e.g. `8.3×`), and % above/below long-run average (e.g. `▲ 42% avg`)
acs.note: "Each loaded preset card" quantifies over 9. Worse, not even ONE is addressable: PresetCard's root is role="button" with no accessible name (its text is the dynamic title/value).

acs.text: Chart is rendered using a Recharts `<LineChart>` inside a `<ResponsiveContainer>` at ~160px height (compact mode)
acs.note: Prescribes Recharts <LineChart>, <ResponsiveContainer> and ~160px. A behaviour tree deliberately cannot express implementation, and should not.

acs.text: A dashed `<ReferenceLine>` is drawn at the long-run average value
acs.note: A dashed <ReferenceLine> is a drawing instruction; it also lives inside SVG with zero ARIA, so no locator exists either.

acs.text: No axis labels are shown in compact mode
acs.note: "No axis labels are shown" is an absence, conditioned on a mode the notation cannot name.

acs.text: Hovering over a data point shows a Recharts custom `<Tooltip>` with: date (formatted via date-fns, e.g. `Jan 2007`), ratio value, and % above/below average
acs.note: No hover verb. The step vocabulary is closed at 8 words (state/opens/activates/sees/shows/attaches/lands/fills) and pointer interaction is not among them. The tooltip is also inside the unaddressable SVG.

acs.text: Date range buttons (`1y / 2y / 5y / 10y / 20y / Max`) are shown below the chart; default is **Max**
acs.note: The six buttons have PERFECT accessible names ("1y"…"Max") and are still unusable: nine PresetCards each render all six, and the notation cannot scope a noun to a region. "default is Max" is marked by className="active" only — no aria-pressed — so the AC is untestable without changing the app.

acs.text: Clicking a date range button filters the visible series client-side using date-fns `subYears` / `isAfter` — no re-fetch
acs.note: Prescribes date-fns; "no re-fetch" is a negative; and the filtered series is inside the unaddressable SVG.

acs.text: The long-run average `<ReferenceLine>` recalculates over the visible date range when the range changes
acs.note: Asserts a recomputed value inside the SVG, related to another control's state.

acs.text: The 9 presets are ordered by theme: Affordability (UK, US, UK Real HPI) → Inflation-adjusted (Real Gold, Real S&P 500, Real Oil) → Cross-asset (Gold vs Equities, UK Property/Gold, BTC vs Gold)
acs.note: Ordering over a collection. The notation has neither.

acs.text: Cards are displayed in a 3-column responsive grid
acs.note: Layout. Correctly outside a behaviour tree, but it is still an AC someone signed off.

acs.text: Clicking anywhere on a loaded preset card scrolls the page to the `#compare` section
acs.note: The trigger is unaddressable (unnamed card) and the effect is a scroll position, which is neither a URL nor a DOM assertion.

acs.text: The numerator dropdown is set to the preset's numerator metric
acs.note: No way to assert a control's CURRENT VALUE — only that a noun is visible or contains text. Radix does surface the selection as the combobox's accessible name, but that makes the noun's identity change with its value, which breaks one-binding-per-noun.

acs.text: The denominator dropdown is set to the preset's denominator metric
acs.note: As 58.

acs.text: The custom comparison fetch is triggered automatically (as if the user had selected both dropdowns manually)
acs.note: FINDING: `contract` is not a free-standing escape hatch — it must hang off a behaviour. Story 3's behaviour is itself unexpressible (57), so this contract has no host and the AC drops out entirely.

acs.text: The full-width chart renders with the preset's data
acs.note: The chart region IS addressable (#compare); its trigger is not, so no behaviour can carry it.

acs.text: Two Radix UI `<Select>` dropdowns are rendered side by side with a ⇄ swap button between them
acs.note: All three controls are asserted visible. "side by side" / "between them" is layout; "Radix UI <Select>" prescribes implementation.

acs.text: Each dropdown lists the 11 comparable metrics: UK House Prices, US House Prices, UK Wages, US Wages, UK CPI, US CPI, Gold, Oil, FTSE 100, S&P 500, Bitcoin
acs.note: FINDING: `provides` RECORDS the 11 labels into the symbol table and nothing asserts them. This is the only collection in the document the notation can carry, and carrying is not checking.

acs.text: The metric selected as numerator is excluded from the denominator dropdown options, and vice versa
acs.note: A negated relation between two nouns that changes as one is used. No shape for any of the three parts.

acs.text: Clicking ⇄ swaps the current numerator and denominator selections; if both are set, the chart re-fetches with swapped values
acs.note: POSITIVE FINDING: the conditional half ("if both are set") is NOT a gap — it splits cleanly into two behaviours with different `given` lines. What blocks it is 58's missing shape: asserting a select's current value.

acs.text: When only the numerator is selected, a prompt "Now select a denominator" is shown in place of the chart
acs.note: The prompt is asserted; "in place of the chart" (the chart's absence) is not.

acs.text: When neither is selected, a prompt "Select two metrics above to see a custom comparison" is shown
When both are selected, the custom comparison chart is rendered (see Story 5)
On both metrics being selected, `GET /api/metrics/ratio?numerator=X&denominator=Y` is fired
acs.note: Wire-level.

acs.text: While fetching, a loading skeleton is shown in the chart area
acs.note: given/when/then has no DURING. Loading states are the most common thing a frontend spec says and the notation cannot say them. The skeleton is also a className-only div.

acs.text: On success, a Recharts `<LineChart>` renders at ~320px height (full mode) with:
acs.note: FINDING: the chart title is specified as a template, `{Numerator label} / {Denominator label}`. The notation has no interpolation, so the general claim degrades to one INSTANCE ("Gold / US CPI"). Also: this single AC line carries seven sub-bullets — the extractor counts it as one, so 46 undercounts the real assertion load. Six of the seven are inside the unaddressable SVG.

acs.text: Date range buttons (`1y / 2y / 5y / 10y / 20y / Max`) below the chart; default **Max**; filtering is client-side
acs.note: As 41. In full mode there is exactly one chart, so scoping the noun to #compare would be enough — the notation just cannot scope.

acs.text: On API error, an inline error message is shown: `⚠ Could not load data.` with a **Try again** button that re-fires the fetch
acs.note: Written in full and it generates. `given ratio:Errored` is unbound because macro-metrics has ZERO .spec.ts files, so no route-mock helper exists to bind to. Kit refuses rather than invent one.

acs.text: Three indicator cards are displayed in a row, each narrower than the preset ratio cards (~1/3 page width)
acs.note: "Three … in a row, each narrower than" — count, layout and a comparative, none expressible.

acs.text: Each loaded card shows: title, current value (e.g. `32.4×` or `4.6%`), and % above/below long-run average (e.g. `+90% above long-run avg`)
acs.note: As 36; IndicatorCard's root is an unnamed <div>.

acs.text: Each card contains a sparkline — a compact Recharts `<LineChart>` with a dashed `<ReferenceLine>` at the long-run average, labelled with the avg value (e.g. `avg (17×)`)
acs.note: Prescribes a Recharts sparkline with a labelled ReferenceLine.

acs.text: Indicator cards are visually distinct from preset ratio cards (muted styling, narrower width) — they provide supporting context, not the primary content
acs.note: Purely visual and comparative. The notation SHOULD fail here — this is a design-review item, not a testable behaviour — but it is still an AC with a checkbox next to it.

acs.text: While loading, a skeleton shimmer fills the card
acs.note: As 92.

acs.text: On error, the card shows `⚠ Unavailable` (no retry for MVP — indicator errors are non-blocking)
acs.note: Written; `ratio:Errored` unbound as at 102. Asserted at the #indicators section, not per card, because individual cards are unaddressable.

acs.text: Each preset card manages its own RTK Query fetch independently; an error on one card does not affect others
acs.note: The INSTANCE is written (one failing region beside a working one). "Each card" / "does not affect others" is a universal negative with no shape. Also prescribes RTK Query.

acs.text: Each indicator card manages its own fetch independently
A failed preset card shows: `⚠ Could not load data. Retry?` with a **Try again** button
acs.note: FINDING (spec vs app): the AC says the card shows "⚠ Could not load data. Retry?". PresetCard.tsx:39-40 renders "⚠ Could not load data." and a separate "Try again" button — the word "Retry?" is nowhere in the component. Encoding the prose is what surfaced it.

acs.text: A failed indicator card shows: `⚠ Unavailable`
Clicking **Try again** on a preset card re-fires that card's fetch only
acs.note: "that card's fetch only" is a negative over the other cards; kept as a contract line so it is counted, not dropped.

acs.text: All other cards on the page remain unaffected by the error
acs.note: A universal negative. Carried as prose on the isolation behaviour so it stays visible.
